summary: Fourteen days of good-quality CGM data (98.7% coverage, 5-minute cadence) show overall time-in-range of 86.0% with above-target variability (CV 32.6%) and a below-range percentage of 5.1% that exceeds typical comfort thresholds. Distinct patterns include excellent overnight-to-dawn control (04:00-07:00 local), a recurring daytime hyperglycemia peak around 16:00 local, several severe hypoglycemia clusters (notably 08-13 and 08-14), and several severe hyperglycemia clusters (08-15 and 08-18) often paired with below-range time on the same day, suggesting oscillation rather than a single one-directional defect. A critical limitation is that zero carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day dataset, which blocks direct evaluation of carb ratios, meal bolus timing, and e-carb strategy, and leaves open whether daytime highs and some overnight lows are driven by unlogged meals, insulin-on-board stacking under a 10-hour duration of insulin action, or dynamic-ISF/automation behavior. No change to any profile or AAPS automation parameter is supported by the current evidence; the most valuable next step is establishing a carbohydrate log to separate these competing explanations.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage 98.7% with 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps (largest 65 minutes), zero invalid or duplicate entries. Zero carbohydrate entries exist across the full 14 days despite clearly meal-shaped glucose excursions. A mid-period Profile Switch to a differently named basal/ISF configuration occurred on 2026-08-13, and an Occlusion plus Pump Error were logged on 2026-08-19.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall time-below-range is 5.1% and coefficient of variation is 32.6%, both indicating meaningful glucose instability. Severe hypoglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and an isolated reading on 2026-08-21. Severe hyperglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18. Days with the highest time-above-range also show elevated time-below-range on the same day (08-14, 08-18), suggesting oscillation rather than a single static defect.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot yet attribute specific hypo/hyper pairs to basal, ISF, automation aggressiveness, or unlogged meals without further separation in later steps.

analysis_steps.findings: Dawn hours (04:00-07:00 local) show excellent control (95.2-98.7% time-in-range). The 00:00-02:00 local window shows the day's highest time-below-range (up to 18.5% at 01:00 local), more consistent with a residual insulin-on-board tail from earlier activity than a live basal defect, since loop statuses show dosing already suspended before these lows. Daytime hours (10:00-18:00 local) show rising time-above-range peaking at 32.1% at 16:00 local, coinciding with the profile's basal step-down from 0.7 to 0.5 U/h at that hour; several Temporary Targets of 135 mg/dL were active during parts of this window and must be excluded as confounds before attributing the pattern to the standing profile.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local; aaps_profile.basal_segments; aaps_profile.target_segments; representative_events Temporary Target entries; representative_loop_statuses insulin_req and iob fields.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate log to confirm or exclude meals as the daytime driver; correction-bolus and SMB contributions are not fully separable from basal contribution in either window.

analysis_steps.findings: ISF is a single flat segment (56 mg/dL/U), consistent with the profile's own naming ('FLAT ISF'); dynamic ISF adjustment (70% factor) produces an effective sensitivity range of roughly 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U in sampled loop statuses, a wide but designed swing. Carb ratio review is fully blocked because zero carbohydrate entries exist in the package; no meal response can be used to validate any ratio segment. DIA of 10 hours is long relative to typical rapid-acting durations and is a plausible contributor to insulin-on-board stacking seen in some correction-response windows, but this cannot yet be separated from automation safety-limit behavior.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.isf_segments; aaps_profile.carb_ratio_segments; aaps_profile.dia_hours; representative_loop_statuses variable_sens values; treatment_summary.carb_entries=0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data blocks carb ratio assessment entirely; DIA-versus-automation-ceiling separation requires automation-stage findings.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled with smb_always_enabled true and both carb-gated activation flags false; given zero logged carbohydrates, UAM is effectively carrying all meal-response duty, confirmed by loop reason strings showing COB:0 alongside active UAM Boost multipliers during clear glucose rises. SMB continued operating during active Temporary Targets, consistent with smb_with_temp_target_enabled true and smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, since none of the logged temporary targets appear to meet the 'high' threshold. No internal inconsistency was found among SMB/UAM settings; min_carbs_required_grams is currently functionally inert given the no-carb-logging pattern, but this is a cosmetic observation, not a safety concern.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings; representative_loop_statuses reason strings; representative_events Temporary Target entries; treatment_summary.carb_entries=0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot determine whether the absence of logged carbohydrates reflects true minimal-carb management or unlogged meals being fully absorbed by UAM.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while dynamic ISF is enabled, a standard non-conflicting pairing; sensitivity_ratio values of 1 are read as neutral rather than disabled. Observed peak enacted basal (4.0 U/h) and peak IOB (5.935 U) during the period remained far below the configured max_basal_u_per_hour (12 U/h) and max_iob_units (25 U) ceilings, meaning these two settings were never binding during the severe hyperglycemia episodes on 08-15, 08-18, and 08-21. An audit-only setting outside the six decision groups, current_basal_safety_multiplier (6.0), appears more consistent with the observed practical ceiling than the profile-level max_basal_u_per_hour, but this cannot be confirmed as the binding constraint without further data. Automation showed protective suspension of dosing before overnight lows, and reactive UAM compensation during unexplained daytime rises, supporting the hypotheses formed in basal_targets rather than indicating an automation defect.
analysis_steps.evidence: representative_loop_statuses sensitivity_ratio, variable_sens, iob, and insulin_req fields; aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings safety multiplier fields; aaps_profile.basal_segments; treatment_summary.total_insulin_u.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot confirm whether current_basal_safety_multiplier meaningfully constrained the 08-15/08-18 spikes or whether unlogged large meals would have overwhelmed even a higher ceiling; sparse loop-status sample limits generalization.

analysis_steps.findings: aaps_profile.analysis_context.meal_strategies is an empty declared list, meaning no prebolus_minutes, immediate_bolus_percent, or e-carb fields have been declared by the user for this period; there is therefore no declared strategy to compare against telemetry. All 24 sampled therapy_response_windows are typed Correction Bolus with COB:0; no meal-typed bolus exists anywhere in the package. Within the correction-only data, two recurring response sub-patterns are visible: high-starting-glucose corrections followed by steep multi-hour drops, and near-normal-starting-glucose corrections that still drift into hypoglycemia by 180-240 minutes, both plausibly explained by IOB stacking, dynamic ISF swings, or unlogged meals without the data available to distinguish them.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared meal strategy exists to compare against execution; no meal-typed bolus events exist to analyze prebolus timing or immediate bolus percentage.

analysis_steps.findings: extended_carb_entries is 0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min is null; no e-carb amount, start offset, or duration is declared or logged anywhere in the package. The carb absorption model settings (min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours) exist but have never been exercised by an actual carbohydrate entry during the period, so they cannot be evaluated against observed absorption.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or regular carb entries exist to assess amount, timing, or duration against observed glucose response.

analysis_steps.findings: The dominant unresolved issue across every stage is the complete absence of carbohydrate logging, which prevents separating meal effects from basal, CR, ISF, and DIA effects in both the overnight low pattern and the daytime 16:00 high pattern. Overnight lows are best explained by residual insulin-on-board tail (automation already showed protective suspension before these lows), not by a live basal defect. Daytime highs at 16:00 local coincide with a basal step-down but are equally explained by unlogged meals met by reactive UAM dosing; the two explanations cannot be separated without carb data. Automation safety ceilings (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units) were never binding during the observed severe excursions, so they are not implicated as a direct cause, though an audit-only safety multiplier outside the decision inventory may be a more relevant practical ceiling for future review. No single profile or AAPS parameter change is supported by current evidence strongly enough to isolate it from these competing explanations; the safe, non-overlapping next step is establishing carbohydrate logging before any dependent insulin-delivery parameter is changed.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consolidated findings from data_quality, safety_overview, basal_targets, profile_cr_isf_dia, automation_smb_uam, automation_sensitivity_limits, meal_bolus_strategy, and meal_ecarbs_absorption.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carbohydrate logging is the single largest gap blocking confident, isolated recommendations across nearly every stage.

strengths: Dawn and early-morning hours (04:00-07:00 local) show excellent control with time-in-range between 95.2% and 98.7%.
Overall time-in-range across the 14-day period is 86.0%, and CGM data quality is high with 98.7% coverage and no invalid or duplicate entries.
Automation repeatedly showed protective behavior, suspending dosing (insulin_req at or near 0) ahead of predicted overnight lows rather than causing them.
Total daily basal insulin is internally consistent with the profile's own labeled design ('16-2u per day').
issues: Time-below-range across the period is 5.1% with a coefficient of variation of 32.6%, both indicating meaningful glucose instability beyond typical targets.

Severe hypoglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21; severe hyperglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18, with several of these days showing elevated time above and below range simultaneously.
A recurring daytime hyperglycemia pattern peaks around 16:00 local (32.1% time-above-range), coinciding with a basal step-down, but cannot be separated from unlogged meal effects.
Zero carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day dataset, which blocks direct evaluation of carb ratios, meal bolus timing, and e-carb strategy.
An Occlusion and Pump Error were logged on 2026-08-19, and a mid-period Profile Switch occurred on 2026-08-13, both of which are confounds for interpreting glucose behavior in those windows.

recommendations.title: Establish carbohydrate logging before further profile or automation changes
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrate entries exist across the full 14-day period, which blocks separation of meal effects from basal, CR, ISF, and DIA effects in both the overnight low pattern and the daytime 16:00 high pattern. This is the single change most likely to improve confidence in every other finding.

The single flat segment appears intentional, matching the profile's own naming convention. Dynamic ISF already modulates effective sensitivity across a 0.5x-2.2x range around this baseline in sampled loop data, and no isolated evidence indicates the flat baseline itself needs adjustment independent of that dynamic modulation.
Overnight lows appear driven by residual insulin-on-board rather than an overly aggressive target, since automation showed protective dosing suspension during these episodes.
Daytime highs are better explained by unlogged meal effects and reactive UAM dosing than by this target value; no isolated evidence supports a change.

A 10-hour DIA is a plausible contributor to insulin-on-board stacking seen in some correction-response windows, but this competes with automation safety-limit behavior as an explanation and cannot yet be isolated. Changing DIA before separating these causes risks unpredictable interaction with dynamic ISF and SMB dosing.

UAM is currently carrying all meal-response duty given zero logged carbohydrates, confirmed by loop reasoning showing COB:0 with active UAM Boost multipliers during glucose rises. No internal inconsistency was found; disabling either setting is not supported without first resolving whether meals are being logged.

parameter_decisions.parameter: Max basal rate and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Observed peak enacted basal (4.0 U/h) and peak IOB (5.935 U) during the period remained far below these ceilings, meaning they were never binding during the severe hyperglycemia episodes on 08-15, 08-18, and 08-21. A separate audit-only safety multiplier outside this decision group may be a more relevant practical ceiling, but that cannot be confirmed as the binding constraint with current data, so no change to these two values is supported.

Autosens disabled alongside dynamic ISF enabled is a standard, non-conflicting pairing. Observed sensitivity_ratio values of 1 are neutral, not disabled autosens. The wide effective sensitivity range (0.5x-2.2x baseline) is consistent with the configured 70% adjustment strength operating as designed, not evidence of a defect.

exceptions.pattern: Corrections starting from high glucose (above 180 mg/dL) followed by steep multi-hour drops of 170 mg/dL or more by 360 minutes
exceptions.suggestion: Flag this pattern for review as a possible overcorrection or insulin-stacking signature rather than a meal-timing issue
exceptions.rationale: The magnitude and delay of these drops exceed what the logged correction dose alone would typically produce, implicating concurrent SMB or insulin-on-board activity rather than the meal-bolus strategy itself

exceptions.pattern: Corrections starting from near-normal glucose (93-127 mg/dL) that still drift into hypoglycemia by 180-240 minutes
exceptions.suggestion: Flag this pattern for review as a possible residual insulin-on-board or DIA-tail signature distinct from the high-start overcorrection pattern
exceptions.rationale: Since the starting glucose was not elevated, the delayed low is more consistent with stacked prior insulin activity than with the correction bolus itself

implementation_steps: Begin logging carbohydrate intake (approximate amounts and timestamps) for at least 7-10 days before making any other change, since this single step unblocks the largest number of unresolved questions.

After the logging period, review whether the 16:00 local hyperglycemia pattern and the 00:00-02:00 local hypoglycemia pattern persist on days without meals near those times before considering any basal or DIA change.
Change only one profile or automation parameter at a time, and observe its effect for several days before making a second change.
Discuss the recurring same-day high-and-low oscillation pattern (as seen on 08-14 and 08-18) with a care team before adjusting any automation aggressiveness setting.
Continue monitoring time-in-range, time-below-range, and coefficient of variation weekly to confirm whether patterns are improving, stable, or worsening.
education: Time-below-range (currently 5.1%) and coefficient of variation (currently 32.6%) are both variability indicators; values above typical comfort thresholds suggest glucose is swinging more than desired, independent of the average glucose level.

Under carb-unaware automation with SMB and UAM enabled, glucose rises with COB:0 can still trigger corrective microboluses; this reactive response is not evidence of a meal being logged, only that the algorithm detected a rise.

Dynamic ISF can substantially widen or narrow the effective sensitivity used for dosing decisions around a flat profile ISF value; this is a designed behavior, not an error, but its magnitude should be considered when interpreting delayed drops after corrections.

A longer duration of insulin action (DIA) can extend how long a prior dose continues to lower glucose, which may contribute to delayed lows several hours after a correction, especially when combined with additional microbolus activity.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; TuneMyBG prepares data for review and does not provide medical advice.
Independently verify every proposed change with a qualified care team before applying it, and make only one change at a time.

Monitor glucose closely after any change, particularly given the severe hypoglycemia clusters observed on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21, and the severe hyperglycemia clusters observed on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18.
Do not change AAPS settings automatically based on this analysis; all changes require manual review and gradual, sequential verification.
